scenes.title: A normal day for Leo
scenes.captureAction: Open on an all-vector night street hook (They look. They leave. Nobody knows why.), then push the camera into Leo's store as day breaks.
scenes.narration: People walk in. They look around. Then… they leave. For Leo, it's becoming a familiar story. He runs a furniture shop in a busy neighborhood. The products are ready. The customers are out there. But after days of trying to bring them back, he's still guessing. Who should he reach? And what should he offer? The clues are already there, in what shoppers browse, what they ask about, and what they buy. Leo just needs a way to connect them.
onScreen: They look. They leave. Nobody knows why.

scenes.title: What Market Metro is
scenes.captureAction: Introduce Market Metro as an AI commerce environment using the actual market view and Observe, Train, Test and Measure stages. Do not show ontology as the product itself.
scenes.narration: Could AI help him figure it out, and bring those customers back? Meet Market Metro: a simulated commerce world where AI agents learn from shopper behavior, build campaigns, and show what happens next.
onScreen: A commerce world for AI agents

scenes.title: The right data for the question
scenes.captureAction: The ontology routes recommendation and inquiry history separately, while distinguishing input features from later outcome labels.
scenes.narration: First, we give the agent a map. That's our ontology. It connects shoppers, products, interactions, and payments into one understandable story. It keeps a product recommendation separate from a general inquiry, and makes sure one purchase isn't counted twice. Now the agent has a clearer picture of what happened, which examples to learn from, and who might be ready to return.

scenes.title: From understanding to action
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: It studies demand, checks available stock, and uses local tools to train two models.

scenes.title: Test before sending
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: Before a campaign goes out, the verifier checks the candidates against fixed rules. Which one produces better outcomes for merchants and PayPal?

scenes.title: The recommendation becomes a purchase
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: Then we follow the campaign into the market. Day thirty-five. A shopper who hasn't purchased in sixteen days receives a recommendation. A ninety-six-dollar side table catches their interest. They buy it. The next day, it arrives. Under fixed rules, that same request went unfilled.

scenes.title: A payment you can trace
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: Here's where PayPal closes the loop. In our demo, that exact order connects to a PayPal Sandbox capture. We can follow the purchase through the payment, the processing fee, and what the merchant receives.

scenes.title: What changed
scenes.captureAction: Show fixed 627 vs agent 643, sixteen highlighted payment icons, and incremental payment volume, merchant contribution and modeled PayPal net.
scenes.narration: And across this market, the difference adds up. Sixteen more retained purchases. Over twenty-three hundred dollars in additional payment volume. More than a thousand dollars in extra merchant contribution. And roughly a hundred fifteen dollars more in modeled PayPal net, after AI cost.

scenes.title: Follow the full trail
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: Want to see how we got there? Open AG Grid. Follow the models, the agent's decisions, the campaign, and the PayPal receipt.

scenes.title: Agentic commerce that learns
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: Leo started with a guess. Now there's a tested campaign, and a trail showing what worked. Market Metro. Agentic commerce that learns.

uploadDraft.title: Market Metro | Agentic Commerce That Learns | PayPal AI Hackathon
uploadDraft.description:
Market Metro turns observed merchant activity into trained models, tested campaigns and traceable PayPal payments. This demo follows one saved 12-store, 600-shopper simulation from Day 1 to a recorded agent decision, purchase and native PayPal Sandbox receipt.

Against fixed rules in that same simulation: 16 more retained purchases, $1,024.86 additional merchant contribution, and $114.96 higher modeled PayPal net after estimated model cost. Merchant contribution includes inventory value. These are simulated outcomes, not actual PayPal profit. The $96 Sandbox capture is an existing order and uses fictitious funds.

Built with PayPal Sandbox, Gemini on Vertex AI, local scikit-learn models, SQLite, Three.js and AG Studio with native AG Grid, AG Charts and a custom PayPal evidence widget. The ontology feed comparison is a separate synthetic-data test.

Source and setup: https://github.com/VinceVence/market-metro
Original code: MIT. Third-party components retain their own licenses.
